questions.stem: A young female weighing 46kg on digoxin with vd-6L/kg Clearance:4.6 L/h. Calculate half-life of digoxin:
questions.solutionHtml:
42h

Formula for half-life is

  • Here, V= volume of distribution, in this case Vd is 46 x 6= 276.
  • CL- clearance= 4.6L/h
  • So putting all this in formula-
  • t1/2= 276 x 0.693/4.6 = 42h.Hence, option C is correct.

questions.answerText: Acute oral overdose results primarily in cerebellar and vestibular symptoms and high doses have been associated with marked cerebellar atrophy
questions.solutionHtml:
Acute oral overdose results primarily in cerebellar and vestibular symptoms and high doses have been associated with marked cerebellar atrophy
  • Option: A. Is correct as Over dose toxicity due to higher plasma concentration of phenytoin produces:

(a) Cerebellar and vestibular manifestations: ataxia, vertigo, diplopia, nystagmus.

(b) Drowsiness, behavioural alterations, mental confusion, hallucinations, disorientation and rigidity.

questions.stem: A 60 years old patient who is a known case of hypertension and diabetes, underwent PCI stent placement for NSTEMI last year. He is currently on aspirin, metoprolol and atorvastatin. He comes for follow-up and his lipid profile is as follows - Total cholesterol 252mg/dl, LDL: 156mg/dl, Triglyceride 158mg/dl and HDL-40 mg/dl. Which drugs can be added based on his lipid profile?EzetimibeEvolocumabGemfibrozilBempedoic acidSelect the correct Answer From the given below Code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1, 2 and 4
  • Patient is having hypertension and diabetes and taking aspirin, metoprolol and atorvastatin, and LDL is still high so it will be a case of MI -ASCVD (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease).
  • In patients with ASCVD the main aim is to decrease LDL. So drugs effective to reduce LDL are ezetimibe, evolocumab and bempedoic acid i.e. Option A is correct.


Goodman & Gilman's, The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No.747

questions.stem: Drug that binds to CD4 and has action on both CCR5 and CXCR4 in tropic HIV infections:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ibalizumab
  • Ibalizumab is a monoclonal antibody that specifically binds to the CD4 receptor on immune cells, preventing HIV from entering the cell by blocking the conformational changes needed for the virus to interact with both CCR5 and CXCR4 co-receptors, making it effective against both CCR5-tropic and CXCR4-tropic HIV strains.


Goodman & Gilman's, The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 14th Edition, Page No.1258

questions.stem: Drug acting on sodium channel and potentiating slow sodium inactivation:
questions.solutionHtml:
Lacosamide
  • Lacosamide is an antiseizure drug and acts by slow inactivation of voltage-gated Na+ channels and to limit sustained repetitive firing, the neuronal firing pattern characteristic of focal seizures.

questions.stem: Inhibitors of Poly ADP ribose polymerase (PARP) are approved for BRCA positive breast cancers. Which among the following drugs is used?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rucaparib
  • Rucaparib is an orally bioavailable inhibitor of PARP1–3. Approved for the treatment of patients with advanced ovarian cancer with BRCA mutations and is used in the maintenance treatment of these patients after a partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy.
